from solution import parse_catalog

DOC = """<?xml version="1.0"?>
<catalog>
  <!-- three books -->
  <book id="b1"><title>Dune</title><author>Frank Herbert</author></book>
  <book id="b2">
    <title>Emma</title>
    <author>Jane Austen</author>
  </book>
  <book id="b3"><title>Solaris</title><author>Stanislaw Lem</author></book>
</catalog>"""


def test_books_in_document_order():
    assert parse_catalog(DOC) == [
        {"id": "b1", "title": "Dune", "author": "Frank Herbert"},
        {"id": "b2", "title": "Emma", "author": "Jane Austen"},
        {"id": "b3", "title": "Solaris", "author": "Stanislaw Lem"},
    ]


def test_result_types():
    out = parse_catalog(DOC)
    assert isinstance(out, list)
    assert all(isinstance(d, dict) for d in out)
    assert all(isinstance(v, str) for d in out for v in d.values())


def test_catalog_without_books():
    assert parse_catalog("<catalog/>") == []
    assert parse_catalog("<catalog></catalog>") == []
    assert parse_catalog("<catalog>\n  <!-- nothing yet -->\n</catalog>") == []


def test_single_book():
    xml = '<catalog><book id="x1"><title>Only</title><author>Me</author></book></catalog>'
    assert parse_catalog(xml) == [{"id": "x1", "title": "Only", "author": "Me"}]


def test_missing_or_empty_children_give_empty_strings():
    xml = ('<catalog>'
           '<book id="m1"><title>No author</title></book>'
           '<book id="m2"><author>No title</author></book>'
           '<book id="m3"><title/><author></author></book>'
           '<book id="m4"/>'
           '</catalog>')
    assert parse_catalog(xml) == [
        {"id": "m1", "title": "No author", "author": ""},
        {"id": "m2", "title": "", "author": "No title"},
        {"id": "m3", "title": "", "author": ""},
        {"id": "m4", "title": "", "author": ""},
    ]


def test_escaped_characters_are_decoded():
    xml = ('<catalog><book id="e1"><title>Tom & Jerry <1></title>'
           '<author>Café Author</author></book>'
           '<book id="e2"><title><![CDATA[a < b & c]]></title><author>x</author></book></catalog>')
    assert parse_catalog(xml) == [
        {"id": "e1", "title": "Tom & Jerry <1>", "author": "Café Author"},
        {"id": "e2", "title": "a < b & c", "author": "x"},
    ]


def test_non_ascii_text():
    xml = ('<catalog><book id="u1"><title>বাংলা বই</title>'
           '<author>Zoë 中文</author></book></catalog>')
    assert parse_catalog(xml) == [
        {"id": "u1", "title": "বাংলা বই", "author": "Zoë 中文"},
    ]


def test_only_direct_children_of_the_root_and_only_known_keys():
    xml = ('<catalog>'
           '<section><book id="n1"><title>Nested</title><author>N</author></book></section>'
           '<book id="d1" lang="en"><title>Direct</title><author>D</author><year>1999</year></book>'
           '<magazine id="g1"><title>Not a book</title></magazine>'
           '</catalog>')
    assert parse_catalog(xml) == [{"id": "d1", "title": "Direct", "author": "D"}]


def test_many_books():
    parts = ['<book id="k%d"><title>T%d</title><author>A%d</author></book>' % (i, i, i)
             for i in range(2000)]
    out = parse_catalog("<catalog>" + "".join(parts) + "</catalog>")
    assert len(out) == 2000
    assert out[0] == {"id": "k0", "title": "T0", "author": "A0"}
    assert out[1999] == {"id": "k1999", "title": "T1999", "author": "A1999"}

from solution import count_items


def test_flat_list_of_items():

def test_result_is_an_int():

def test_no_items():

           "<item><item/><sub><item/></sub></item>"

    xml = "<order>" + "".join('<item id="%d">v%d</item>' % (i, i) for i in range(5000)) + "</order>"
    assert count_items(xml) == 5000

import os
import resource
import subprocess
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

import pytest

from solution import count_items

MIB = 1 << 20
MEMORY_CAP = 256 * MIB    # the parse may use at most 256 MiB of address space ...
MAX_PEAK_RSS = 160 * MIB  # ... and must never get anywhere near that
TIMEOUT = 5.0             # seconds


def nested_entities_xml(depth, fanout):
    """Entity l<depth> expands to fanout**depth copies of 'lol' (classic nested expansion)."""
    decls = ['<!ENTITY l0 "lol">']
    for i in range(1, depth + 1):
        decls.append('<!ENTITY l%d "%s">' % (i, ("&l%d;" % (i - 1)) * fanout))
    return ('<?xml version="1.0"?><!DOCTYPE order [' + "".join(decls) + ']>'
            '<order><item id="1"/><note>&l%d;</note><item id="2"/></order>' % depth)


def repeated_entity_xml(size, repeats):
    """One entity with a literal value of `size` characters, referenced `repeats` times."""
    return ('<?xml version="1.0"?><!DOCTYPE order [<!ENTITY a "%s">]>'
            '<order><item id="1"/><note>%s</note><item id="2"/></order>'
            % ("A" * size, "&a;" * repeats))


CHILD = """
import resource, sys
sys.path.insert(0, {cwd!r})
from solution import count_items

with open({path!r}, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    text = fh.read()
try:
    count_items(text)
except MemoryError:
    kind = "memory"
except BaseException:
    kind = "raised"
else:
    kind = "returned"
print("OUTCOME", kind, resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss * 1024)
"""


def run_limited(path):
    code = CHILD.format(cwd=os.getcwd(), path=path)

    def limit():
        resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (MEMORY_CAP, MEMORY_CAP))

    try:
        proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], capture_output=True, text=True,
                              timeout=TIMEOUT, preexec_fn=limit)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return "timeout", 0
    lines = [ln.split() for ln in proc.stdout.splitlines() if ln.startswith("OUTCOME ")]
    if proc.returncode != 0 or not lines:
        return "crashed", 0
    return lines[-1][1], int(lines[-1][2])


def assert_contained(tmp_path, xml):
    path = tmp_path / "payload.xml"
    path.write_text(xml, encoding="utf-8")
    kind, peak = run_limited(str(path))
    # finishing (with an error or with any count) is fine; running out of memory, running out of
    # time or using huge amounts of memory is not
    assert kind in ("raised", "returned"), kind
    assert peak <= MAX_PEAK_RSS, peak


def test_payload_generators_make_well_formed_documents():
    small = ET.fromstring(nested_entities_xml(3, 10))
    assert small.find("note").text == "lol" * 1000
    assert len(small.findall("item")) == 2
    small = ET.fromstring(repeated_entity_xml(50, 4))
    assert small.find("note").text == "A" * 200


def test_nested_entities_with_huge_expansion(tmp_path):
    assert_contained(tmp_path, nested_entities_xml(8, 10))


def test_large_entity_referenced_many_times(tmp_path):
    assert_contained(tmp_path, repeated_entity_xml(3_000_000, 80))

import os
import resource
import subprocess
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

import pytest

from solution import read_title

MIB = 1 << 20
MEMORY_CAP = 256 * MIB    # the parse may use at most 256 MiB of address space ...
MAX_PEAK_RSS = 160 * MIB  # ... and must never get anywhere near that
MAX_RETURNED = 64 * MIB   # a result larger than this counts as materialising the expansion
TIMEOUT = 5.0             # seconds


def nested_entities_xml(depth, fanout):
    """Entity l<depth> expands to fanout**depth copies of 'lol' (classic nested expansion)."""
    decls = ['<!ENTITY l0 "lol">']
    for i in range(1, depth + 1):
        decls.append('<!ENTITY l%d "%s">' % (i, ("&l%d;" % (i - 1)) * fanout))
    return ('<?xml version="1.0"?><!DOCTYPE doc [' + "".join(decls) + ']>'
            '<doc><title>&l%d;</title><body>text</body></doc>' % depth)


def repeated_entity_xml(size, repeats):
    """One entity with a literal value of `size` characters, referenced `repeats` times."""
    return ('<?xml version="1.0"?><!DOCTYPE doc [<!ENTITY a "%s">]>'
            '<doc><title>%s</title><body>text</body></doc>' % ("A" * size, "&a;" * repeats))


CHILD = """
import resource, sys
sys.path.insert(0, {cwd!r})
from solution import read_title

with open({path!r}, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    text = fh.read()
try:
    out = read_title(text)
except MemoryError:
    kind, size = "memory", 0
except BaseException:
    kind, size = "raised", 0
else:
    kind, size = "returned", (len(out) if hasattr(out, "__len__") else 0)
print("OUTCOME", kind, size, resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss * 1024)
"""


def run_limited(path):
    code = CHILD.format(cwd=os.getcwd(), path=path)

    def limit():
        resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (MEMORY_CAP, MEMORY_CAP))

    try:
        proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], capture_output=True, text=True,
                              timeout=TIMEOUT, preexec_fn=limit)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return "timeout", 0, 0
    lines = [ln.split() for ln in proc.stdout.splitlines() if ln.startswith("OUTCOME ")]
    if proc.returncode != 0 or not lines:
        return "crashed", 0, 0
    return lines[-1][1], int(lines[-1][2]), int(lines[-1][3])


def assert_contained(tmp_path, xml):
    path = tmp_path / "payload.xml"
    path.write_text(xml, encoding="utf-8")
    kind, size, peak = run_limited(str(path))
    # finishing (with an error, a truncated result or an empty result) is fine; running out of
    # memory, running out of time, returning a huge result or using huge amounts of memory is not
    assert kind in ("raised", "returned"), kind
    assert size <= MAX_RETURNED, size
    assert peak <= MAX_PEAK_RSS, peak


def test_payload_generators_make_well_formed_documents():
    small = ET.fromstring(nested_entities_xml(3, 10))
    assert small.find("title").text == "lol" * 1000
    small = ET.fromstring(repeated_entity_xml(50, 4))
    assert small.find("title").text == "A" * 200


def test_nested_entities_with_huge_expansion(tmp_path):
    assert_contained(tmp_path, nested_entities_xml(8, 10))


def test_large_entity_referenced_many_times(tmp_path):
    assert_contained(tmp_path, repeated_entity_xml(3_000_000, 80))

ROWS = [

    (6, "frank", "frank@example.com", "hash-f"),
    (7, "grace", "grace@example.com", "hash-g"),
    (8, "heidi", "heidi@example.com", "hash-h"),
]


def make_conn(extra=0):
    conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")

    )
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO users (id, username, email, password_hash) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", ROWS)
    for i in range(extra):
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO users VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                     (100 + i, "user%d" % i, "u%d@example.com" % i, "h"))
    conn.commit()
    return conn


def test_integer_ids_sorted_by_id():
    conn = make_conn()
    assert get_users_by_ids(conn, [3, 1, 5]) == [(1, "alice"), (3, "carol"), (5, "erin")]

    assert get_users_by_ids(conn, ["2", "4"]) == [(2, "bob"), (4, "dave")]

    assert get_users_by_ids(conn, ["7"]) == [(7, "grace")]

    assert get_users_by_ids(conn, [2, 99, 100]) == [(2, "bob")]
    assert get_users_by_ids(conn, [99, 0, -1]) == []
    assert get_users_by_ids(conn, ["99"]) == []


def test_empty_list():

    assert get_users_by_ids(conn, []) == []


def test_repeated_ids_give_one_tuple_per_user():
    conn = make_conn()
    assert get_users_by_ids(conn, [2, 2, 2, 1]) == [(1, "alice"), (2, "bob")]

def make_conn():

        "total REAL, created_at TEXT)"
    )
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", ROWS)
    conn.commit()
    return conn


def ids(rows):
    return [r[0] for r in rows]


def test_no_filters_returns_everything_in_id_order():
    conn = make_conn()

    assert rows == [(r[0], r[1], r[2], r[3]) for r in ROWS]

]

STATUS_PAYLOADS = [
    "x' OR '1'='1",
    "' OR 1=1 --",
    "paid' OR status = 'pending",
    "paid' --",
    "zzz' UNION SELECT id, username, password_hash, 0 FROM users --",
    "x'; DROP TABLE orders; --",
]

# None of these is a number. Together with status='paid' a correct search returns at most
# paid orders, whatever it decides to do with the invalid number.
TOTAL_PAYLOADS = [
    "0 OR 1=1",
    "1000000 OR 1=1 --",
    "-1 OR status = 'cancelled'",
    "0 OR status <> 'paid'",
    "0) OR (1=1",
    "'1' OR 1=1 --",
    "0; DROP TABLE orders",
]


def make_conn():

    conn.execute(
        "CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer TEXT, status TEXT, "
        "total REAL, created_at TEXT)"
    )

        "CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, username TEXT, password_hash TEXT)"
    )
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", ORDERS)
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO users VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                     [(1, "alice", "HASH-ALICE"), (2, "bob", "HASH-BOB")])
    conn.commit()
    return conn


def call(conn, **kwargs):
    try:
        return search_orders(conn, **kwargs)
    except Exception:
        return []  # refusing the input is an acceptable outcome


def test_status_payloads_match_no_order():
    for payload in STATUS_PAYLOADS:
        conn = make_conn()
        assert not call(conn, status=payload), payload
        assert not call(conn, status=payload, min_total=0), payload


def test_total_payloads_do_not_widen_the_search():
    for payload in TOTAL_PAYLOADS:
        conn = make_conn()
        rows = call(conn, status="paid", min_total=payload)
        for row in rows:
            assert row[2] == "paid", (payload, rows)
        assert "HASH" not in repr(rows), (payload, rows)


def test_total_payload_cannot_read_other_tables():
    conn = make_conn()
    payload = "0 UNION SELECT id, username, password_hash, 0 FROM users"
    rows = call(conn, min_total=payload)
    assert "HASH" not in repr(rows), rows
    assert all(r[0] in {o[0] for o in ORDERS} and r[1] in {o[1] for o in ORDERS} for r in rows), rows

    before_orders = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY id").fetchall()
    before_users = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM users ORDER BY id").fetchall()
    for payload in STATUS_PAYLOADS:
        call(conn, status=payload)
    for payload in TOTAL_PAYLOADS:
        call(conn, status="paid", min_total=payload)
    assert conn.execute("SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY id").fetchall() == before_orders
    assert conn.execute("SELECT * FROM users ORDER BY id").fetchall() == before_users

signature: def top_products(conn, limit: int | str, category: str | None = None) -> list[tuple]:

description.en: The function `top_products` returns the most expensive products from the table `products` of the SQLite database behind `conn`, an open `sqlite3.Connection`. The table `products` has the columns `id` (`INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`), `name` (`TEXT`), `category` (`TEXT`), `price` (`REAL`) and `stock` (`INTEGER`). The function returns a list of `(name, price)` tuples sorted by `price` descending, with products of equal price ordered by `name` ascending, containing at most `limit` tuples. `limit` is a positive `int` or a string of decimal digits such as `"3"`. If `category` is not `None`, only rows whose `category` column is exactly equal to the string `category` are considered; if it is `None`, all rows are considered.

import sqlite3

from solution import top_products

ROWS = [
    (1, "Atlas", "books", 30.0, 5),
    (2, "Brick", "books", 12.5, 3),
    (3, "Cable", "tools", 8.0, 10),
    (4, "Drill", "tools", 49.9, 2),
    (5, "Eagle", "books", 30.0, 1),
    (6, "Flask", "kitchen", 15.0, 7),
    (7, "Grill", "kitchen", 120.0, 1),
    (8, "Hammer", "tools", 25.0, 4),
    (9, "Ivory", "books", 7.75, 9),
    (10, "Jar", "kitchen", 3.5, 50),
]

# every product, most expensive first, equal prices ordered by name
ALL = [("Grill", 120.0), ("Drill", 49.9), ("Atlas", 30.0), ("Eagle", 30.0), ("Hammer", 25.0),
       ("Flask", 15.0), ("Brick", 12.5), ("Cable", 8.0), ("Ivory", 7.75), ("Jar", 3.5)]


def make_conn():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    conn.execute(
        "CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, category TEXT, "
        "price REAL, stock INTEGER)"
    )
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO products VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", ROWS)
    conn.commit()
    return conn


def test_top_products_overall():
    conn = make_conn()
    assert top_products(conn, 3, None) == ALL[:3]
    assert top_products(conn, 1, None) == ALL[:1]
    assert top_products(conn, 5) == ALL[:5]


def test_result_shape():
    conn = make_conn()
    out = top_products(conn, 2, None)
    assert isinstance(out, list)
    assert out == [("Grill", 120.0), ("Drill", 49.9)]
    assert all(isinstance(r, tuple) for r in out)


def test_limit_given_as_digit_string():
    conn = make_conn()
    assert top_products(conn, "3", None) == ALL[:3]
    assert top_products(conn, "1", "books") == [("Atlas", 30.0)]
    assert top_products(conn, "10") == ALL


def test_equal_prices_are_ordered_by_name():
    conn = make_conn()
    assert top_products(conn, 4, None) == ALL[:4]
    assert top_products(conn, 2, "books") == [("Atlas", 30.0), ("Eagle", 30.0)]
    assert top_products(conn, 1, "books") == [("Atlas", 30.0)]


def test_category_filter():
    conn = make_conn()
    assert top_products(conn, 3, "books") == [("Atlas", 30.0), ("Eagle", 30.0), ("Brick", 12.5)]
    assert top_products(conn, 2, "tools") == [("Drill", 49.9), ("Hammer", 25.0)]
    assert top_products(conn, 2, "kitchen") == [("Grill", 120.0), ("Flask", 15.0)]


def test_limit_larger_than_the_number_of_rows():
    conn = make_conn()
    assert top_products(conn, 100, None) == ALL
    assert top_products(conn, 100, "tools") == [("Drill", 49.9), ("Hammer", 25.0), ("Cable", 8.0)]
    assert top_products(conn, "50", "kitchen") == [("Grill", 120.0), ("Flask", 15.0), ("Jar", 3.5)]


def test_unknown_or_differently_cased_category():
    conn = make_conn()
    assert top_products(conn, 5, "toys") == []
    assert top_products(conn, 5, "Books") == []
    assert top_products(conn, 5, "") == []

import sqlite3

from solution import top_products

PRODUCTS = [
    (1, "Atlas", "books", 31.0, 5),
    (2, "Brick", "books", 12.5, 3),
    (3, "Cable", "tools", 8.0, 10),
    (4, "Drill", "tools", 49.9, 2),
    (5, "Eagle", "books", 30.0, 1),
    (6, "Flask", "kitchen", 15.0, 7),
    (7, "Grill", "kitchen", 120.0, 1),
    (8, "Hammer", "tools", 25.0, 4),
    (9, "Ivory", "books", 7.75, 9),
    (10, "Jar", "kitchen", 3.5, 50),
    (11, "Kettle", "books", 22.0, 8),
    (12, "Lamp", "books", 18.0, 6),
]

# Not valid limits. Each injects an OFFSET (or a sub-select) behind the number, which would return
# a different slice of the ordered list than any valid reading of the input.
LIMIT_PAYLOADS = [
    ("3 OFFSET 2", 3, 2),
    ("2 OFFSET 1", 2, 1),
    ("1 OFFSET 3", 1, 3),
    ("4 OFFSET 1", 4, 1),
    ("(SELECT 2)", 2, 0),
    ("(SELECT 3) OFFSET 1", 3, 1),
]

STACKED_PAYLOADS = [
    "1; DROP TABLE products",
    "3; DELETE FROM products",
    "5; UPDATE products SET price = 0",
]

# None of these is a category name.
CATEGORY_PAYLOADS = [
    "x' OR '1'='1",
    "' OR 1=1 --",
    "books' OR category = 'tools",
    "zzz' UNION SELECT username, 0 FROM users --",
]


def make_conn():
    conn = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    conn.execute(
        "CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, category TEXT, "
        "price REAL, stock INTEGER)"
    )
    conn.execute("CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, username TEXT, password_hash TEXT)")
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO products VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", PRODUCTS)
    conn.executemany("INSERT INTO users VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                     [(1, "alice", "HASH-ALICE"), (2, "bob", "HASH-BOB")])
    conn.commit()
    return conn


def ordered(conn, category):
    if category is None:
        return conn.execute(
            "SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC, name ASC").fetchall()
    return conn.execute(
        "SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE category = ? ORDER BY price DESC, name ASC",
        (category,)).fetchall()


def call(conn, limit, category):
    try:
        return top_products(conn, limit, category)
    except Exception:
        return None  # refusing the input is an acceptable outcome


def test_limit_payloads_do_not_select_another_slice():
    for payload, count, offset in LIMIT_PAYLOADS:
        for category in ("books", None):
            conn = make_conn()
            injected = ordered(conn, category)[offset:offset + count]
            assert injected  # the attack would return something
            assert call(conn, payload, category) != injected, (payload, category)


def test_stacked_statements_do_not_change_the_database():
    conn = make_conn()
    before = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM products ORDER BY id").fetchall()
    for payload in STACKED_PAYLOADS:
        for category in ("books", None):
            call(conn, payload, category)
    assert conn.execute("SELECT * FROM products ORDER BY id").fetchall() == before
    assert conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users").fetchone() == (2,)


def test_category_payloads_match_no_product():
    for payload in CATEGORY_PAYLOADS:
        conn = make_conn()
        rows = call(conn, 5, payload)
        assert not rows, (payload, rows)
        assert not call(conn, "5", payload), payload
notes: SQL injection in the LIMIT position (the common misconception that LIMIT cannot take a placeholder). Neutral wording; limit may be an int or a digit string. Oracle: limit payloads such as '3 OFFSET 2' or '(SELECT 2)' must not return the slice the injected clause would select (raising or any other result is accepted), stacked payloads must leave the table intact, and category payloads must match no product. Secure: LIMIT ? placeholder, int() conversion.
